breakfast.name: Strapatsada (Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes and Feta)
breakfast.description: Traditional Greek scrambled eggs with juicy tomatoes and creamy feta cheese, embodying the Greek philosophy of quality ingredients over complexity
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 10-15 minutes until moisture evaporates and tomatoes become jammy
Crack eggs into the pan and gently scramble into the cooked tomato mixture
Cook for 3-4 minutes until eggs are set but still creamy
Fold in crumbled feta cheese
Season with dried oregano, salt, and pepper
Serve immediately with crusty bread
breakfast.notes: The key is not to overcook the eggs - they should remain creamy and not rubbery. Use ripe, flavorful tomatoes for best results
breakfast.fun_fact: Strapatsada reflects the Greek breakfast philosophy: focus on quality, fresh ingredients rather than quantity. This dish has been enjoyed in Greece for generations
alternatives: Add sautéed peppers along with tomatoes
Add fresh herbs like dill or parsley
Include pan-fried saganaki (fried cheese) on the side

lunch.name: Fish Souvlaki (Grilled Fish Skewers)
lunch.description: Ancient Greek grilled fish skewers with vegetables, served in pita bread with tzatziki sauce. Traditional Mediterranean cooking method documented since Homer's time
instructions: Mix olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for marinade
Cut fish into chunks and marinate for 30 minutes
Thread fish alternately with peppers and onion on skewers
Grill 3-4 minutes per side over high heat until charred
Serve in pita with tzatziki, tomatoes, and lettuce
lunch.notes: Firm fish varieties withstand grilling better than delicate white fish. Marinating adds flavor and keeps fish moist
lunch.fun_fact: Souvlaki is the Greek equivalent of kebab, an ancient cooking method documented since Homer's time. Street food and restaurant staple throughout Greece

dinner.name: Moussaka (Baked Eggplant and Meat Lasagna)
dinner.description: Greek layered baked dish with eggplant, meat sauce and béchamel topping
ingredients: Salt, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, oregano to taste
instructions: Salt eggplant slices and let rest 30 minutes to remove moisture
Heat olive oil and fry eggplant and potato slices until golden; set aside
Brown meat with onion, add garlic, fry 1 minute
Add tomatoes, wine, broth, cinnamon, nutmeg, oregano; simmer 30 minutes
Make béchamel: melt butter, add flour, stir 1 minute, slowly add milk whisking constantly
Season béchamel with salt, pepper, nutmeg
Layer in baking dish: potatoes, eggplant, meat sauce, repeat; top with béchamel
Bake at 180°C for 60 minutes until golden
dinner.notes: Moussaka improves when made a day ahead and reheated
dinner.fun_fact: Dates back to Ottoman palace cuisine, perfected in 1920s Greece
alternatives: Add pine nuts to meat layer

dinner.name: Pastitsio (Greek Layered Pasta)
dinner.description: Greek baked pasta with meat sauce and béchamel - Greek lasagna
instructions: Brown ground meat in oil with onion and garlic
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, wine, cinnamon, oregano
Simmer 15 minutes until sauce thickens
Season with salt and pepper
Meanwhile, cook pasta al dente, drain and toss with butter
Make béchamel: melt butter, add flour, cook 1 minute
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth
Cook stirring constantly until thickened (5-7 minutes)
Remove from heat, let cool slightly
Whisk egg yolks, then temper by slowly adding hot béchamel while whisking
Stir egg mixture back into béchamel, add half the cheese
In baking dish, layer: pasta, meat sauce, pasta, béchamel
Top with remaining cheese
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40-45 minutes until golden and bubbling
Let rest 10 minutes before serving
dinner.notes: Can be assembled ahead and refrigerated before baking
dinner.fun_fact: Pastitsio is the most beloved dish in Greek cuisine, served at family gatherings and celebrations
